linked-nodes.title: Follow the links
linked-nodes.intro: Compare traversal with insertion into a singly linked list.
linked-nodes.scope: Single-threaded singly linked list; allocation and ownership are omitted. Insertion is O(1) once the preceding node is known.

steps.title: Start at head
steps.explanation: Head identifies A. Each node stores a value and the next node reference.

steps.title: Follow one link
steps.explanation: Read A.next to reach B; a linked list does not provide constant-time access by index.

steps.title: Reach the tail
steps.explanation: Read B.next to reach C. C.next is null, so traversal finishes.

steps.title: Keep the old link
steps.explanation: We already hold a reference to A. Finding A would itself require traversal.

steps.title: Link X first
steps.explanation: Set X.next = A.next, preserving access to B.

steps.title: Reconnect A
steps.explanation: Set A.next = X. The chain is now A → X → B, with no nodes lost.

stacks-queues.title: Same arrivals, different departures
stacks-queues.intro: A, B and C arrive in that order. Predict which leaves first.
stacks-queues.scope: Abstract push/pop and enqueue/dequeue behavior; storage strategy and thread safety are separate choices.

steps.title: Three arrivals
steps.explanation: The stored items are A, B and C.

steps.title: First removal
steps.explanation: C leaves first under LIFO.

steps.title: Drain the collection
steps.explanation: The complete departure order is C → B → A.

steps.title: Three arrivals
steps.explanation: The stored items are A, B and C.

steps.title: First removal
steps.explanation: A leaves first under FIFO.

steps.title: Drain the collection
steps.explanation: The complete departure order is A → B → C.

recursion.title: Walk a small tree
recursion.intro: Compare preorder and postorder: the shape is unchanged, but when we emit each node changes.
recursion.scope: Binary tree with three nodes. These snapshots group calls together; traversal time is O(n), and call-stack space depends on tree height.

steps.title: Begin at root
steps.explanation: Emit A before recursing into B.

steps.title: Return from left leaf
steps.explanation: B has no children, so its recursive call returns to A.

steps.title: Finish the right subtree
steps.explanation: C returns to A, then the root call finishes.

steps.title: Begin at root
steps.explanation: Do not emit A yet. Recurse into B first.

steps.title: Return from left leaf
steps.explanation: B has no children, so its recursive call returns to A.

steps.title: Finish the right subtree
steps.explanation: C returns to A, then the root call finishes.

sorting.title: Watch insertion sort grow a sorted prefix
sorting.intro: Compare how input order changes the amount of shifting.
sorting.scope: Each step is one outer-loop insertion, not one comparison. Insertion sort is O(n²) in the worst case; sorted input takes O(n) comparisons with this implementation.

steps.title: Initial array
steps.explanation: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix, beginning with the first item.

steps.title: Insert item 2
steps.explanation: Insert 3 into the sorted prefix, shifting 1 larger item(s) right.

steps.title: Insert item 3
steps.explanation: Insert 2 into the sorted prefix, shifting 2 larger item(s) right.

steps.title: Insert item 4
steps.explanation: Insert 1 into the sorted prefix, shifting 3 larger item(s) right.

steps.title: Initial array
steps.explanation: Insertion sort grows a sorted prefix, beginning with the first item.

steps.title: Insert item 2
steps.explanation: Insert 3 into the sorted prefix, shifting 0 larger item(s) right.

steps.title: Insert item 3
steps.explanation: Insert 2 into the sorted prefix, shifting 1 larger item(s) right.

steps.title: Insert item 4
steps.explanation: Insert 4 into the sorted prefix, shifting 0 larger item(s) right.

graphs.title: Breadth-first search keeps a frontier
graphs.intro: Watch a FIFO queue find the shortest unweighted path, or exhaust the reachable component.
graphs.scope: Directed, unweighted graph. Early exit occurs when the target is discovered; weighted shortest paths need different reasoning.

steps.title: Enqueue A
steps.explanation: Mark A discovered when enqueuing it. The queue starts with A.

steps.title: Expand A
steps.explanation: Remove A and discover B. Record B’s parent as A.

steps.title: Expand B
steps.explanation: Discover C from B, record its parent, and reconstruct A → B → C.

steps.title: Enqueue A
steps.explanation: Mark A discovered when enqueuing it. The queue starts with A.

steps.title: Expand A
steps.explanation: Remove A and discover B. Record B’s parent as A.

steps.title: Expand B
steps.explanation: B has no undiscovered neighbors. The queue empties without discovering C.

binary-search-tree.title: Use ordering to choose a branch
binary-search-tree.intro: At every node, compare the target with the stored key.
binary-search-tree.scope: Distinct keys and a valid binary-search-tree ordering. Search is O(h); an unbalanced tree can have height n.

steps.title: Compare with 8
steps.explanation: Target 6 is smaller than 8: follow the left child.

steps.title: Compare with 3
steps.explanation: Target 6 is greater than 3: follow its right child.

steps.title: Compare with 6
steps.explanation: The key matches. Return this node.

steps.title: Compare with 8
steps.explanation: Target 5 is smaller than 8: follow the left child.

steps.title: Compare with 3
steps.explanation: Target 5 is greater than 3: follow its right child.

steps.title: Compare with 6
steps.explanation: 5 is less than 6, but 6 has no left child. The search ends.
